findings.title: Recovery owns two incompatible notions of unknown
findings.trigger: A recovery decision combines an outer-worker observation with writerBoundaryState during the launch or cancellation transition.
findings.impact: The inner writer boundary is modeled as stopped or unknown, but the outer worker is modeled only as alive or not alive. Combining them lets outer uncertainty authorize cleanup of the inner writer's sole fence, so the one-writer invariant is bypassable at the ownership seam.
findings.evidence: deriveWriterState preserves unknown for missing or unverifiable writer.json, while outerWorkerView maps pid null and unavailable identity directly to alive false. cancel then combines false with inner not_started equals stopped and performs terminal cleanup.
findings.suggestion: Use the same minimal three-state vocabulary at the outer boundary and centralize its interpretation. Callers may report running for alive, conservative unknown for unknown, and perform cleanup only for stopped; no new workflow engine or durable state is needed.

positive_observations: Repair 2 otherwise reuses the existing file-first artifacts and driver state model; no new daemon, database, lease, or workflow engine was introduced.
The smallest complete correction is one shared tri-state view plus caller guards rather than a new recovery subsystem.
limitations: Host-created child sessions and a stronger non-Linux start-identity mechanism remain separate P2 concerns.
